acceptance: A schema represents methodology version, capability profile, S/M/L dataset vector, workload blocks, weights, oracles, and reference vector.

The result identity binds BenchBox revision, platform/adapter/driver versions, rendered SQL and parameters, dataset hashes, hardware, OS, topology, tuning, cache, warmup, repetition, and result-consumption policy.
Throughput identity includes concurrency, session schedule, active interval, and per-session configuration.
Canonical serialization and content hashes make manifests replayable and tamper-evident.
Compatibility tests reject undeclared or non-comparable methodology changes.
context: Implements the proposed cross-benchmark score architecture. Preserve official TPC metrics as separate outputs. The ADR's numerical weights, size vectors, concurrency points, and M4 reference are pilot hypotheses until the methodology-freeze item closes.
description: Define the versioned score-methodology, dataset-profile, scored-query, schedule, and result-evidence schemas. The cohort identity must bind software, hardware, deployment, data, SQL, tuning, cache, warmup, result-consumption, and concurrency state.
